title: Use of Tracer Dyes to Label Neural Projections to Lower Urinary Tract Organs
author: Janet R Keast
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.w2xfgfn
materials: Prepare tracer dye solutions: Fluorogold or Fast Blue (each 2% w/v in sterile water).
Shave and clean the ventral abdomen.

steps.title: Anesthetize and Prepare Animal
steps.instruction: Prepare the animal for surgery using anesthesia and supportive care.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize animal with 2.5% isoflurane in oxygen (or as required for maintenance).
Place animal on a heated pad.

steps.title: Expose Injection Site
steps.instruction: Perform a midline incision in the skin and muscle, then gently move organs to visualize the required injection site.

steps.title: Microinject Tracer Solution
steps.instruction: Inject sterile tracer solution using a Hamilton Neuros Syringe attached to a 33G needle, holding the needle in place for ~5 seconds after ejection to ensure spread and minimize leakage.

substeps.instruction: For bladder body (dome) injections: inject bilaterally on dorsal and ventral aspects (total volume ~5 µl).
For bladder trigone or dorsal aspect of the proximal urethra: perform single injections (maximum 0.3 µl per injection).

steps.title: Post-Injection Care and Closure
steps.instruction: Clean the surgical site and close the incision.

substeps.instruction: Wash all injection sites with sterile saline.
Close the muscle and skin using approved procedures.
Administer analgesics and monitor animal during postoperative period as per local approved procedure.

steps.title: Tissue Harvest and Fixation
steps.instruction: Fix the animals and collect tissues 5-14 days after surgery to analyze tracer dye distribution.

substeps.instruction: Remove tissues of interest, typically including dorsal root ganglia (DRG) from L1, L2, L6 and S1 spinal levels and the pelvic ganglia (major pelvic ganglia).
Remove lower urinary tract tissues for microscopic validation of the tracer injection site.
